questions.question: When a linear program is set up for Excel Solver, what do the changing cells represent?
options: The values of the objective function
The right-hand sides of the constraints
The coefficients of the constraints
The decision variables of the model

questions.question: A modeller builds an LP in Excel and runs Solver. Which statement describes what Solver does with the spreadsheet?
options: It adds nonnegativity when the problem plainly requires it
It solves exactly the model in the sheet and adds nothing
It detects constraints that are missing from the sheet
It rounds variables that represent counts to whole numbers

questions.question: The Simplex LP solving method in Excel Solver is meant for continuous linear models. With changing cells B1 (holding $x_1$) and B2 (holding $x_2$), which sheet fits this method?
options: Objective =3*B1+2*B2, constraint formula =B1+B2 at most 4
Objective =B1+5*B2, constraint formula =B1^2+B2 at most 9
Objective =3*B1/B2, constraint formula =B1+B2 at most 4
Objective =B1*B2, constraint formula =B1+B2 at most 4

questions.question: A transport planner models the number of buses $x$ as a changing cell, states only $x\ge0$ and the seat constraint, and solves with Simplex LP. What may Solver report for $x$?
options: An error message, since buses cannot be split in real life
A whole number of buses, as buses are counted in whole units
A fractional number of buses, as integrality was not stated
The fractional value, rounded up to the next whole number

questions.question: Why should a solution reported by Excel Solver be checked against the original constraints of the mathematical model?
options: A typing error can make the sheet differ from the intended model
Solver ignores any bounds placed directly on the changing cells
Solver may have changed the right-hand sides during the run
Passing the constraint check is what confirms that the plan is optimal

questions.question: For the LP $\max\,4x_1+3x_2$ (profit) subject to $x_1+x_2\le5$ (machine hours), $2x_1+x_2\le8$ (labour hours), $x_1,x_2\ge0$, the sheet has changing cells B1 (holding $x_1$) and B2 (holding $x_2$). Which formula belongs in the objective cell?

For the LP $\max\,4x_1+3x_2$ (profit) subject to $x_1+x_2\le5$ (machine hours), $2x_1+x_2\le8$ (labour hours), $x_1,x_2\ge0$, the sheet has changing cells B1 (holding $x_1$) and B2 (holding $x_2$), and cell D2 is used for the labour-hours constraint. How should this constraint be entered?
options: D2 =2*B1+B2, which must be at least 8
D2 =B1+B2 for labour, capped at 8
D2 =2*B1+B2, plus the bound B1 at most 8
D2 =2*B1+B2, which must not exceed 8

questions.question: A cost model is $\min\,2x_1+3x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\ge4$, $0\le x_1\le6$, $0\le x_2\le6$. The modeller leaves Solver's direction on maximization. Which result does Solver report?
options: $(4,0)$ with value 8
$(0,6)$ with value 18
$(0,4)$ with value 12
$(6,6)$ with value 30

questions.question: A model is $\min\,x_1+2x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\ge3$, $x_1\le5$, $x_1,x_2\ge0$. The sheet omits the nonnegativity restrictions. What does Solver report?
options: $(5,-2)$ with value 1
$(3,0)$ with value 3
$(0,3)$ with value 6
$(5,0)$ with value 5

questions.question: An LP requires $x_2\le10$ (stock limit), with $x_2$ in changing cell B2. Instead of a separate formula cell, the modeller enters this as a bound on B2 itself. Is the model correctly represented?
options: No: every constraint needs its own formula cell
Yes: a bound on a changing cell states the constraint
No: Simplex LP ignores bounds on the changing cells
Yes, but only if $x_2$ is also restricted to integers

questions.question: A continuous maximization LP is entered in Solver, but the modeller also restricts the changing cells to integers by mistake. How does the reported optimal value compare with the correct LP optimum?
options: It is always equal, as integrality only affects rounding
It is always higher, as the model is more restrictive
It is never higher, and it may well be strictly lower
It is always strictly lower, as integers are restrictive

questions.question: A decision $y$ must be 1 (open a depot) or 0 (do not open). The modeller enters only the bounds $0\le y\le1$ on its changing cell. What can Solver return for $y$?
options: Any value from 0 to 1, including fractions like 0.4
Only 0 or 1, as Simplex LP returns corner points
Only 0 or 1, since the bounds allow nothing else
Only 1, as the bounds push $y$ to the top value

questions.question: For the LP $\max\,4x_1+3x_2$ (profit) subject to $x_1+x_2\le5$ (machine hours), $2x_1+x_2\le8$ (labour hours), $x_1,x_2\ge0$, the labour formula is typed as =B1+2*B2 instead of =2*B1+B2 (with changing cells B1 (holding $x_1$) and B2 (holding $x_2$)). What does Solver report, and is it feasible for the original LP?
options: $(3,2)$ with value 18, feasible for the original model
$(5,0)$ with value 20, feasible for the original model
$(2,3)$ with value 17, feasible for the original model
$(5,0)$ with value 20, exceeding the labour limit by 2

questions.question: For the LP $\max\,4x_1+3x_2$ (profit) subject to $x_1+x_2\le5$ (machine hours), $2x_1+x_2\le8$ (labour hours), $x_1,x_2\ge0$, Solver reports $(3,2)$ with profit 18. The modeller then notices that a demand limit $x_1\le2$ was omitted from the sheet. What is the optimum once it is added?
options: $(3,2)$ with profit 18
$(2,2)$ with profit 14
$(2,3)$ with profit 17
$(2,4)$ with profit 20

questions.question: For the LP $\max\,4x_1+3x_2$ (profit) subject to $x_1+x_2\le5$ (machine hours), $2x_1+x_2\le8$ (labour hours), $x_1,x_2\ge0$, the machine-hours constraint is entered with the wrong direction, as at least 5 instead of at most 5. What does Solver report, and how does it compare with the original constraints?
options: $(4,0)$ with 16, meeting all the original constraints
$(0,8)$ with 24, exceeding the machine hours by 3
$(3,2)$ with 18, the correct optimum, unaffected
$(0,5)$ with 15, meeting all the original constraints

questions.question: A cost model $\min\,2x_1+3x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\ge4$, $x_1,x_2\ge0$ is entered in Solver with the minimization direction checked, and Solver reports that the objective is unbounded. Which omission explains this?
options: The nonnegativity of $x_1$ and $x_2$ is missing
The upper bounds on $x_1$ and $x_2$ are missing
The constraint $x_1+x_2\ge4$ is missing from the sheet
The integer restrictions on $x_1$ and $x_2$ are missing

questions.question: A school must transport 130 pupils: a big bus has 50 seats and costs 400, a small bus has 30 seats and costs 300. With numbers of buses as changing cells, what are the optimal costs without and with integer restrictions?
options: Continuous 1040; integer 1200 with three big buses
Continuous 1040; integer 1100 with two big, one small
Continuous 1100; integer 1100 with two big, one small
Continuous 1040; integer 800 with two big buses

questions.question: A blend must contain exactly 10 tonnes: $\min\,3x_1+5x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2=10$, $x_1\le6$, $x_1,x_2\ge0$. The equality is typed as at most 10. What does Solver report, and what is the correct optimum?
options: Reports $(6,4)$ with cost 38; correct is the same
Reports $(0,0)$ with cost 0; correct $(10,0)$ with 30
Reports $(0,0)$ with cost 0; correct $(6,4)$ with 38
Reports $(10,0)$ with cost 30; correct $(6,4)$ with 38
